paras: The Memphis manhunt for George Morgan was a search by posses of German residents in Memphis, Tennessee, on April 15, 1903, for Morgan, a Black man accused of shooting and killing a German brewery worker, Adolph Heinz, with the stated aim of lynching him. The posses did not find him, and three months later he was arrested in St. Louis, where he denied the shooting. An Associated Press dispatch about the hunt ran in white newspapers across the South and Midwest.

Heinz was described as 'a native German' employed at the Tennessee Brewery in Memphis. The wire account said Heinz refused to honor an order Morgan presented for a pail of beer, and that Morgan then shot and killed him. The same dispatch described Morgan as 'a negro, with a picturesque police record.'

On learning of the killing, German residents of the part of the city near the brewery 'immediately formed posses' and searched for Morgan 'with the avowed purpose of lynching him.' The size of the posses was not reported, and no officers are mentioned as taking part. At a late hour Morgan had not been captured, and the dispatch reported that 'quiet prevails in the vicinity of the brewery.'

On July 12, 1903, St. Louis police, acting on information from the Memphis police, arrested Morgan for murder. He was charged with shooting 'Adolph Heintz of the Memphis Brewing company,' denied the shooting, and said he would return to Memphis without requisition. No report of an indictment, trial or verdict was found in the coverage.

The Associated Press text, dated Memphis April 15 or 16, appeared on April 16 in the Montgomery Advertiser, the Birmingham Age-Herald, the Richmond Times Dispatch, the Savannah Morning News, the Indianapolis Journal and the Beatrice Daily Express in Nebraska. It ran the next day in the Louisville Courier-Journal, the Americus Times-Recorder and the Norfolk Weekly News-Journal, and as late as April 20 in the Atlanta Constitution and Wisconsin's Vilas County News. Several papers carried a shortened version that dropped the police-record phrase and the closing line about Morgan still being at large.

Headline writers set nationality against race: 'Germans After a Negro' in Indianapolis, 'Germans Searching for Negro Slayer' in Nebraska, and 'GERMANS SEARCHING FOR NEGRO MURDERER' in Savannah. Others put the shooting first, as in the Birmingham Age-Herald's 'NEGRO KILLS GERMAN,' whose subhead called Heinz a 'Saloonkeeper,' and the Courier-Journal's 'KILLED BY NEGRO,' with the subhead 'Brewery Employe Shot Down For Refusing To Fill the "Can."' Georgia papers headed it 'Pail of Beer Caused Murder' or 'Pot of Beer Caused Murder.' None of these versions commented on the posses' declared intent to lynch, and the Vilas County News reworded it so that 'the friends of the dead man' were the ones searching.
The July arrest was carried in the Omaha Daily Bee under the headline 'ALLEGED ASSASSIN IS HELD,' which included Morgan's denial. No coverage of the episode was found in the Black press.

The April wire said the shooting followed Heinz's refusal to honor an order for a pail of beer, while the July St. Louis report, based on Memphis police information, said Heintz was shot 'while he was paying off employees.' The reports also differ on the spelling of the dead man's name and on his employer, the Tennessee Brewery in April and the Memphis Brewing company in July. Morgan's guilt was stated as fact in the April dispatch, but he denied the shooting after his arrest.

reader.title: Memphis manhunt for George Morgan
bases: Posses of German residents hunted George Morgan, a Black man accused of killing a brewery employee, 'with the avowed purpose of lynching him', but did not find him; a threatened lynching (A1, A8).

The posses searched for Morgan intending to lynch him in retaliation for the shooting, but he was not caught and was arrested in St. Louis three months later, so no one was killed (A1, A13); the posses' size is not given.

The posse hunt and lynching intent rest on one Associated Press dispatch reprinted widely (A1, A2, A8); a separate St. Louis dispatch in July independently confirms that Morgan was wanted for shooting Heinz but does not mention the posses (A13).

accounts.label: Associated Press wire from Memphis
accounts.gist: Morgan shot and killed Heinz after Heinz refused to honor his order for a pail of beer; German residents near the brewery formed posses to find and lynch him; he had not been captured at a late hour.

accounts.label: St. Louis dispatch (Memphis police information)
accounts.gist: Morgan, wanted in Memphis, was arrested for murder, charged with shooting Heintz of the Memphis Brewing company while Heintz was paying off employees; Morgan denied the shooting.

framing.detail: Papers ran the AP text under headlines that set nationality against race, 'Germans Searching for Negro Slayer' and 'Germans After a Negro', and reported the avowed lynching aim without comment.
The Louisville Courier-Journal headlined 'KILLED BY NEGRO' with the subhead 'Brewery Employe Shot Down For Refusing To Fill the "Can."'
The Omaha Bee's July follow-up was headed 'ALLEGED ASSASSIN IS HELD' and gave Morgan's denial.

versions.value: Heinz refused to honor an order presented by Morgan for a pail of beer
Heintz was shot 'while he was paying off employees'

conflicts.note: The April wire was written the day of the killing, with Morgan at large; the July St. Louis report rests on information from the Memphis police. Neither is clearly better evidence.
Spelling variants of one name; the employer names differ between the April and July reports.

versions.value: Wire states as fact that Morgan shot and killed Heinz

conflicts.note: The accusation was never tested in any report found.
